QF.id: AIFM CII Investment Process and Governance_34

question.text: Per the Code of Conduct for AIF Managers and their key management personnel (SEBI AIF Regulations), which of the following is EXPLICITLY required?

answer.text: Guarantee minimum annual returns to investors
Share investee-company confidential information with competitors for price discovery
Record in writing, the investment, divestment and other key decisions, together with appropriate justification for such decisions
Avoid all regulatory compliance that impedes speed

explanation.text: The Logic: The SEBI Code of Conduct for AIF Managers and KMPs explicitly requires: 'Record in writing the investment, divestment and other key decisions, together with appropriate justification for such decisions'. This creates an evidentiary trail for fiduciary review, CTR audits, and investor grievance cases. The Trap: Guarantee returns is prohibited in AIFs. Sharing CI violates confidentiality obligations. Avoiding compliance is absurd. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the Code of Conduct identically. III-A/C Compliance exams test this documentation obligation too. Manager's Pro-Tip: Investment memos should be LONG-FORM (10-15 pages) not summary — they become your defence in SEBI adjudication. Include dissent views from IC members who voted against: if a deal goes sour, dissent-capture protects the majority-approval team.
